title: Goal: Name the ≃+ Packaging Mathlib Stops Short Of
content: The file's docstring poses the OQ-04 question: construct a named additive-group isomorphism $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{\cong} S^1$ induced by Euler's exponential map $t \mapsto e^{it}$. The answer takes the form of `addCircleEquivAdditiveCircle : AddCircle (2 * π) ≃+ Additive Circle`. Mathlib v4.26.0 already provides the topological bijection (`AddCircle.homeomorphCircle' : AddCircle (2 * π) ≃ₜ Circle`) and the homomorphism law (`AddCircle.toCircle_add`) — but no combined `≃+`. This file is exactly that assembly step. Structurally trivial; the only subtle obstruction is a propositional bridge between `AddCircle.toCircle` (general T) and `Real.Angle.toCircle` (T = 2π specialization) which `homeomorphCircle'` uses as its forward map.
mathContext: Target: $\text{AddCircle}(2\pi) \xrightarrow{\simeq_+} \text{Additive Circle}$, where $\text{Additive Circle}$ is the multiplicative group $S^1 \subseteq \mathbb{C}^\times$ wrapped in Mathlib's type alias to expose multiplication as addition.

title: §0 Motivation: Why a Bridge Lemma Is Needed at All
content: The §0 section docstring (lines 76-93) lays out the two Periodic.lift constructions that motivate the bridge: `AddCircle.toCircle` (general T parameter, defined as `(scaled_exp_map_periodic T).lift` and yielding `Circle.exp ((2π/T) * x)` on representatives) versus `Real.Angle.toCircle` (T = 2π specialization, defined as `Circle.periodic_exp.lift` and yielding `Circle.exp x` on representatives by `rfl`). A casual reader might assume these are the same function — and at T = 2π they ARE, but only propositionally. The cited Mathlib reference (`SpecialFunctions/Complex/Circle.lean:168` in v4.26.0) pins down exactly which bearer `homeomorphCircle'` uses: `Real.Angle.toCircle`. The design choice this file makes — using `AddCircle.toCircle` as the canonical forward map of the new `≃+` — is what forces the bridge: we want the named `≃+` to compose with the general `AddCircle.toCircle_*` lemma family (`toCircle_zero`, `toCircle_add`, `injective_toCircle`), so we cannot just adopt `Real.Angle.toCircle` as the forward map.
mathContext: Choice of canonical bearer: $\text{AddCircle.toCircle}_T$ (parameterized over $T$) vs $\text{Real.Angle.toCircle}$ (fixed at $T = 2\pi$). The former is the natural target for general-$T$ lemma reuse; the latter is what Mathlib's existing $\text{homeomorphCircle}'$ uses internally.
prerequisites: Periodic functions and their quotient lifts

title: §0: The Propositional Bridge addCircle_toCircle_eq_angle_toCircle
content: The non-trivial step in the whole file. Mathlib v4.26.0 has TWO distinct (but propositionally equal at T = 2π) lifts of `Circle.exp` from $\mathbb{R} \to \text{Circle}$ through the AddCircle quotient: (1) `AddCircle.toCircle` (general T), defined via `(scaled_exp_map_periodic T).lift`, which on representatives evaluates to `Circle.exp ((2π/T) * x)`; (2) `Real.Angle.toCircle` (T = 2π only), defined via `Circle.periodic_exp.lift`, which on representatives is literally `Circle.exp x` (by rfl). At T = 2π the `(2π)/(2π) = 1` reduction collapses them, but it's a `div_self` step — not definitional. The bridge is a 4-line proof: `induction x using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on`, then `rw [AddCircle.toCircle_apply_mk, div_self (positivity), one_mul]; rfl`. Why this matters: `AddCircle.homeomorphCircle'` uses `Real.Angle.toCircle` as its `toFun`, so reusing its `symm_apply_apply` / `apply_symm_apply` proofs requires translating between the two bearers. The bridge does exactly that.
mathContext: Two Periodic.lift constructions: $\text{AddCircle.toCircle}_T(\bar{x}) = \exp((2\pi/T) \cdot x)$ vs $\text{Real.Angle.toCircle}(\bar{x}) = \exp(x)$. At $T = 2\pi$, $2\pi/2\pi = 1$ collapses them propositionally but not definitionally.

title: §1: addCircleEquivAdditiveCircle — The AddEquiv Construction
content: Defines `addCircleEquivAdditiveCircle : AddCircle (2 * π) ≃+ Additive Circle` as a four-field `AddEquiv` record. `toFun x := Additive.ofMul (AddCircle.toCircle x)` — wraps the canonical quotient bearer through the multiplicative-to-additive type alias. `invFun y := AddCircle.homeomorphCircle'.symm (Additive.toMul y)` — the symm of Mathlib's existing topological bijection. The three obligations are discharged via named-lemma chains: `left_inv` uses the bridge to convert `AddCircle.toCircle` into `Real.Angle.toCircle`, then `homeomorphCircle'.symm_apply_apply` closes; `right_inv` does the same on the other side via `apply_symm_apply`, with `rfl` cleaning up the `Additive.ofMul ∘ toMul = id` round-trip; `map_add'` rewrites with `AddCircle.toCircle_add` then `rfl` translates `*` on `Circle` to `+` on `Additive Circle` (the type alias makes them definitionally the same operation).
mathContext: AddEquiv structure: a bijection $f : G \to H$ between additive groups satisfying $f(x + y) = f(x) + f(y)$. Here $G = \text{AddCircle}(2\pi)$, $H = \text{Additive Circle}$ (the multiplicative group $S^1$ presented additively).

title: §2: @[simp] API — Forward and Inverse Maps Exposed
content: Two @[simp]-tagged API lemmas (both `rfl`-provable by construction). `addCircleEquivAdditiveCircle_apply` says the forward map IS exactly `Additive.ofMul ∘ AddCircle.toCircle` — i.e., applying the equiv unwraps to the canonical quotient bearer. `addCircleEquivAdditiveCircle_symm_apply` says the inverse IS exactly `homeomorphCircle'.symm ∘ Additive.toMul` — i.e., the inverse unwraps to Mathlib's existing topological symm. These are the rewrites downstream users need: when they see `addCircleEquivAdditiveCircle x` in a goal, simp rewrites it to `Additive.ofMul (AddCircle.toCircle x)`, which then composes with all the existing `AddCircle.toCircle_*` lemmas (`toCircle_zero`, `toCircle_add`, `injective_toCircle`, etc.).
mathContext: API design: `@[simp]` lemmas exposing the underlying definitional structure of a packaged equivalence, so downstream proofs can pattern-match against the underlying maps rather than the wrapper.

title: §3: Connection to the Sibling Universal-Cover Formalization
content: The closing summary connects this Mathlib-quotient-side packaging back to the project's parallel universal-cover formalization in `EulerIdentityOQ01OQ01OQ01.lean`. That sibling file proves the analogous claim for the project's own `circleMap : ℝ → ℂ` packaged as `circleHom : Multiplicative ℝ →* ℂˣ` (0 axioms, 0 sorries, 241 LOC). Its §8 summary explicitly states 'kernel is 2π·ℤ (so S¹ ≅ ℝ/2πℤ)' but stops short of constructing the `AddEquiv` — that's exactly what this file delivers. The two formalizations are complementary: the sibling uses the universal cover (ℝ as a Lie algebra mapping multiplicatively onto S¹), and this file uses the quotient (AddCircle as ℝ modulo the kernel). Together they exhibit S¹ as a 1-parameter Lie group from both perspectives.
mathContext: Two equivalent characterizations of $S^1$ as a Lie group: (1) image of universal cover $\mathbb{R} \xrightarrow{\exp(i \cdot)} S^1$ (sibling formalization), (2) quotient $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z} \xrightarrow{\simeq_+} S^1$ (this file).
